## TL;DR

The latest review found no code bugs. It rejected the handoff evidence because the captures came from an earlier tree, and the Agents dialog shot used an ambiguous selector. I corrected the shot plan to use the unique accessible name for the engineer Skills button and wait for the modal before highlighting it. This report records the latest review cycle and does not treat previous captures as evidence for the current tree.

## Work and rationale

The implementation adds “Close dialog” as the accessible name for the Agents Skills dialog close control, and names each Agent card skills button using that agent's name. The regression test checks both source controls. The QA note documents the keyboard and contrast pass that informed the fix. No implementation finding was raised by either review round.

The latest review identified two evidence problems: the screenshots were tied to an earlier source identity, and the dialog capture could not open the modal because its selector matched six buttons. The shot plan now targets `button.agent-skills-add[aria-label="Add skills to engineer"]`, waits for `.am-modal`, and highlights that modal. Work, Settings, and Releases remain direct route captures. RepoOS will capture the declared shots during the new handoff against the checked tree.

A prior test run also exposed test contamination in `servers-command.test.ts`: tests with mocked remote execution could still use live HTTP discovery and see unrelated Tailscale hosts. I isolated those cases by supplying a null HTTP discovery stub wherever the test relies on mocked remote execution. The targeted test file passed all 15 tests after that change.

## Approaches tried

I first updated the shot selector, but the subsequent review evidence still contained the old selector and old captures. The review's capture plan fingerprint confirmed the update had not reached the plan used by that attempt. I then reissued `repoos update 1184 --shots` with all four routes, a unique button selector, and an explicit `waitFor` on the dialog. I inspected the resulting task view to confirm the new selector and wait step were present before proceeding.

I did not try to repair screenshots manually or claim the previous screenshots represented the current source tree. The next handoff is the mechanism that captures the declared shots against the current checked tree.

## Challenges and blockers

The earlier unscoped test run was interrupted by a queued turn and did not complete. During the previous scoped check, remote validation ran the tests and the local test step was consequently skipped; build, formatting, lint, contrast, artifact checks, and UI smoke passed. The targeted `servers-command.test.ts` run passed locally. The scoped check for this handoff is being run after the shot-plan correction; its result will be recorded by the RepoOS check and handoff evidence.

The review also noted that dialogs and menus beyond the Agents Skills dialog were outside the documented deeper keyboard walkthrough. The task's code changes and regression test are limited to the concrete Agents accessible-name findings; no broader dialog behavior bug was identified in review.

## Key learnings

A UI shot plan is part of the evidence, so selectors must be unique and state transitions should be awaited explicitly. A source tree identity matters as much as the route: a correct screenshot from an older tree cannot verify a current change. Test doubles also need to isolate adjacent discovery mechanisms, or a test that mocks one source can still depend on live machine state through another.
